overview: Pragmatic stepped-wedge trial in the eight disease-site clinics: after a 3-month baseline, pairs of clinics switch from usual referral to opt-out automatic referral triggers every 3 months, in an order randomised by the trial statistician, until all eight use triggers after 15 months; outcomes come from routine records with 90 days of follow-up.
population: Adults aged 18 and over with an advanced solid tumour under the care of one of the eight clinics who meet at least one trigger criterion during the trial periods; the first trigger per patient defines entry. Patients already known to specialist palliative care or enrolled in hospice care are excluded.
exposure: An automatic referral to the specialist palliative care clinic generated by the electronic health record when a trigger is met (new stage IV lung, pancreatic or gastric cancer; start of second-line systemic therapy; two unplanned admissions within 60 days; documented performance status 3 or worse), sent unless the oncologist opts the patient out within 5 working days; compared with usual referral at the oncologist's discretion.
procedures: Informatics builds and tests the trigger rules before the first step and runs them silently in usual-care periods, so eligible patients are identified the same way in both conditions. In trigger periods the palliative care nurse calls each referred patient to explain the referral and offer an appointment; the patient may decline. Opt-outs and declines are recorded with a reason. Outcomes are extracted from admission, clinic and death records by an analyst who does not see the step schedule until the analysis.

outcomes.name: Days alive and out of hospital in 90 days
outcomes.measure: 90 minus days in hospital minus days after death, from admission and death records
outcomes.why: Time at home is what patients and families value, and it is available for every eligible patient from routine data.

outcomes.name: First specialist palliative care visit within 12 weeks
outcomes.measure: Proportion of trigger-eligible patients with a first visit within 12 weeks
outcomes.why: The direct effect of the triggers; shows whether a null result reflects no change in referral.

outcomes.name: Aggressive care at the end of life
outcomes.measure: Among patients who die within 12 months of entry: systemic therapy in the last 14 days, intensive care in the last 30 days, or more than one emergency visit in the last 30 days
outcomes.why: Care that patients with advanced cancer often do not want.

outcomes.name: Waiting time for a new palliative care appointment
outcomes.measure: Days from referral to first appointment for all referrals, by month
outcomes.why: Extra referrals could lengthen waits for patients who need care most.

feasibility: The trigger volume (planned at about 120 patients a month) is confirmed on 2025 records before the first step; the clinic sees about 30 new patients a week, and the added nurse time covers calls and triage; waiting time is reviewed monthly by an oversight group that can slow the rollout.
biasMitigation: Order of clinic switching randomised by the trial statistician
Eligible patients identified by the same silent rules in both conditions
Outcome extraction blind to the step schedule

biasFlags.label: Time trends in referral practice
biasFlags.note: Handled by period effects in the model and by randomising the switching order.

biasFlags.label: Contamination before a clinic switches
biasFlags.note: Oncologists may learn the criteria early; referral rates in usual-care periods are monitored.

biasFlags.label: Identification of eligible patients
biasFlags.note: The same silent rules identify eligible patients in both conditions.

parsimony.simplestPath: One primary outcome from routine data, one pre-specified mixed model, and eight clinics in four steps.

theoreticalFramework: None; the question is the effectiveness of a referral change under usual conditions. An implementation framework is left to a later process evaluation.
summary: Stepped-wedge trial in eight clinics over five periods; one primary outcome, one secondary, one process and one balancing measure.
